beginner.summary: For developers and testers who know JSON and basic HTTP and are new to CouchDB. Covers running Apache CouchDB 3.x in Docker, the HTTP API with curl, databases and documents, revisions and 409 conflicts, bulk operations, key range queries, attachments, Mango queries and indexes, map and reduce views, document modelling, users and database security, configuration, backups, and a small registration data store capstone.
prerequisites: Reads and writes JSON and understands HTTP methods and status codes
Uses a terminal and can run commands in a shell on Windows, macOS or Linux
Has Docker Desktop or Docker Engine installed and can pull images
outcomes: Run CouchDB 3.x and perform every CRUD operation with curl, handling revisions and 409 errors
Query data with _all_docs ranges, Mango selectors with indexes and map-reduce views
Model documents, secure users and databases and tune settings through ini files and the _config API
Back up, restore and verify a small CouchDB application

intermediate.summary: For developers who have built basic CouchDB applications and now need synchronisation and production-ready design. Covers the changes feed and its filters, one-shot and continuous replication, the replicator scheduler, revision trees and conflict handling, view lifecycle and tuning, partitioned databases, index selection, validation functions, JWT and other authentication, TLS and CORS, client libraries, PouchDB offline sync, compaction, and an offline-first capstone.
prerequisites: Completes the beginner level or can create documents, Mango indexes and views with curl
Reads Python or JavaScript well enough to write short scripts
Can run several Docker containers with a compose file
outcomes: Build reliable replication and changes-feed consumers that resume after failure
Detect, resolve and design away document conflicts
Tune views, Mango indexes and partitions, and protect data with validation, JWT, TLS and CORS
Deliver an offline-first application synchronised with CouchDB through PouchDB

advanced.summary: For engineers who run or design CouchDB clusters in production. Covers shards, replicas and quorums, cluster bootstrap with Docker Compose, choosing q and n, resharding, 202 responses and consistency, node failure and maintenance mode, HAProxy, write and view performance, Mango at scale, search with Nouveau or Clouseau, metrics and logs, compaction tuning, disaster recovery, hardening, Kubernetes with Helm, rolling upgrades, troubleshooting, and a multi-region capstone.
prerequisites: Completes the intermediate level or has run CouchDB replication and views in a project
Understands Linux administration, networking basics and containers
Can read logs and write shell or Python scripts for tests and automation
outcomes: Build, size, reshard and operate a multi-node CouchDB cluster with a load balancer
Measure and tune writes, views and Mango queries with evidence
Monitor, secure, back up and upgrade a cluster with tested runbooks
Design and prove a multi-region replicated deployment with measured recovery
